Theorem
[Closed-manifold heat kernel] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0417, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0418, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0419, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0420 ↗ def:chow-ii-heat-fundamental-solution ↗ lem:chow-ii-duhamel-closed 1. appe:1.10\group Heat Kernels

On a closed manifold the fundamental solution is unique, symmetric, positive, and has mass one. If $\mathscr H_t f(x)=\int _M h(x,y,t)f(y)\, d\mu (y)$, then \[ \mathscr H_{t_2}\mathscr H_{t_1}=\mathscr H_{t_1+t_2},\qquad h(x,y,t_1+t_2)=\int _M h(x,z,t_2)h(z,y,t_1)\, d\mu (z). \] The IVP $(\partial _t-\Delta )u=F$, $u(\cdot ,0)=f$, is represented by \[ u(x,t)=\int _Mh(x,y,t)f(y)d\mu (y)+\int _0^t\! \int _Mh(x,y,t-s)F(y,s)d\mu (y)ds. \]
